title: Negative for my 'radius ~2.5 sw' reading: doubling the waste's trait kernel (sw 0.4 -> 0.8) on the same fresh seed does not widen the waste vortices' trait cloud, it collapses it to near the kind-blind level (radius 0.39 vs 1.0 at t=5000-6000); the mutation step relative to sw, not sw alone, sets how far the population spreads
summary: c58's trait3d world with the standard waste (ew 0.25, mut_dt 50, dm 0.4), seed 15 / mut_seed 15, T=6000, waste arm at sw 0.4 and at sw 0.8 with identical draws. Per 1000 t, cloud radius: sw 0.4 0.17, 0.33, 0.47, 0.58, 0.83, 1.00; sw 0.8 0.18, 0.27, 0.31, 0.34, 0.32, 0.39 (kind-blind twins on seeds 3-10: 0.26-0.48). Mean distance from the ancestor: 0.12 -> 1.19 against 0.11 -> 0.51. Classes held by >= 3 vortices 31 against 18; first-time dominants after t=3000 6 against 2. A single mutation (step dm 0.4) lowers the waste factor G from 1 to exp(-dm^2/2sw^2) = 0.61 at sw 0.4 but only to 0.88 at sw 0.8, so a mutant's escape advantage is much smaller with the wide kernel and the population stays close to neutral. My earlier reading in 20261028T0006 and 20261028T0326 (the plateau radius ~1 is set by an escape distance of ~2.5 sw) is therefore wrong as a scaling. The bound must come from how the escape advantage (ew, dm/sw) balances mixing and drift. This experiment does not decide that.

finding.operator: width sw of the kind-specific waste's trait kernel
finding.control: same seed and mutation draws at sw 0.4
finding.result: cloud radius at t=5000-6000: 1.00 (sw 0.4) vs 0.39 (sw 0.8); mean distance from ancestor 1.19 vs 0.51; classes >= 3 vortices 31 vs 18

limits: One seed, T=6000, no twin of its own (twins on other seeds stay at radius 0.26-0.48). dm was not varied, so the dm/sw reading is a proposal. The saturation result itself (20261028T0326) is unaffected; only its proposed cause changes.
